title: October stargazing: the best time to see Saturn, meteors from Halley's Comet
byline: AccuWeatherFollowBrian LadaMon, September 28, 2026 at 6:31 PM UTCAdd us on Google
excerpt: Saturn reaches opposition in early October, offering its best viewing of the year, before the Orionid meteor shower brings shooting stars from debris left behind by Halley’s Comet.
content:
Longer autumn nights will give skywatchers more time to look up in October. The month features a variety of astronomy events, including the best time of the year to view Saturn and one of autumn's top meteor showers.

Saturn opposition: Oct. 4

Saturn will be one of the highlights of the night sky in early October as the planet reaches opposition, marking the best time of the year to see the ringed planet.

Opposition occurs when Saturn is directly opposite the sun from the perspective of Earth. Around this time, the planet rises in the east near nightfall, remains visible throughout the night and eventually sets in the west around daybreak.

No telescope is needed to spot Saturn, although using one can reveal the planet's iconic rings.

Although Saturn reaches opposition on Oct. 4, skywatchers do not need to circle one specific night on the calendar. The planet will remain an excellent target throughout the month, giving people the flexibility to choose an evening with favorable weather.

Orionid meteor shower: Oct. 21-22

Shooting stars will streak across the late-October sky when the Orionid meteor shower peaks on the night of Oct. 21 into the early morning of Oct. 22.

Under ideal conditions, up to 20 meteors per hour may be visible, making the Orionids one of the better meteor showers of autumn. The best viewing generally comes after midnight.

The shower gets its name because the meteors appear to originate from the same area of the sky as the constellation Orion. However, shooting stars can streak across many different parts of the sky, not just near Orion.

The Orionid meteor shower can be traced to debris from Halley's Comet. Each year, Earth passes through debris left behind during previous passes of the famous comet, with tiny particles burning brightly as they enter the atmosphere.

Oct. 25-26: Hunter's Moon

October will end with a full moon shining brightly on the night of Oct. 25 into Oct. 26.

The October full moon is commonly known as the Hunter's Moon, a seasonal nickname traditionally tied to the time of year when hunting became easier after fields had been cleared during the harvest.

Other nicknames for October's full moon include the Falling Leaves Moon, Freezing Moon and Migrating Moon.
